title: Bank Rate on 1 January 1844 and on each day it changed, 1844-1914
source: Bank of England, 'A millennium of macroeconomic data for the UK' (version 3.1): sheet 'D1. Official Interest Rates' (Bank Rate 1833-1972 ...), daily
series: date (ISO 8601): 1 January 1844 and each day on which the rate differs from the previous row of the sheet; bank_rate: the new rate, per cent a year
license: The workbook asks users to cite the underlying sources ('When using this data, please cite this source'). The Bank of England publishes it as a research dataset; a subset is stored here for teaching, with attribution to the Bank of England and to the authors of the series.
notes: Workbook SHA-256 4c23dd392a498691eac92659aec283fb43f28118bd80511dc87fc595974195eb (the copy used for Chapters 19-22). The 1856-1858 rows agree with boe_millennium_bank_rate_1856_1858 (Chapter 22). The sheet dates the rise to 9 per cent 11 May 1866 and to 10 per cent 12 May, and the fall to 8 per cent 16 August 1866; Andréadès (1909, p. 360) says 10 per cent from 11 May to 6 August (goldstandard_facts rows an_10pct, an_aug6). The chapter follows the Bank's table.
citation: Bank of England, A Millennium of Macroeconomic Data for the UK, v3.1 (R. Thomas and N. Dimsdale, 2017), sheet D1
